fatal_errors: The proposed Cr addition does not reconstruct the target intervention: liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
The initial material is incorrectly treated as an existing W–Cu composite rather than a single-BCC WTaVTi alloy whose Ti/V-rich channels are selectively replaced by Cu.
The mechanism omits selective Ti extraction, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, and formation of the approximately 300 nm W-rich passivating interlayer.
No quantitative processing, thermal-service, or helium-irradiation boundaries are provided.
The cited evidence concerns Cu–diamond composites and does not validate Cr alloying in W–Cu, its proposed phonon-coupling mechanism, or irradiation performance.
The falsification experiment tests only generic thermal-conductivity improvement and cannot distinguish improved wetting from the target bicontinuous-channel and interfacial-layer mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis shares only the broad objective of improving heat transport through better interfacial bonding. It misses the target material, intervention, architecture, and irradiation comparison. The target uses molten-Cu dealloying to convert Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels in WTaVTi into aligned, nearly pure Cu channels while retaining a continuous RHEA network and forming a W-rich interface. The generated answer instead proposes unspecified Cr alloying and supplies no alloy content, temperature, duration, pressure, architecture, or service limits. Its evidence is an unsupported transfer from Cu–diamond systems. Although a treated-versus-untreated conductivity comparison is minimally falsifiable, it neither evaluates helium swelling/blistering nor establishes the claimed interfacial mechanism.
